findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Known pre-capture information loss still permits duplicate dispatch after native resource failure and checkpoint restore
findings.smallest_reproduction: probe_native.py: create following desk; save original ledger; dispatch and settle run.1; call reader.pinned through deep(994) or deep(995) at default recursion limit 1000; native RecursionError leaves pending raw tuple, no retained unread entries; replace execution-owned mapping value with saved BudgetLedger.from_dict checkpoint; dispatch same admitted action.
findings.actual_result: Native CPython 3.12.3 depths 994/995: pending [(4, tuple)], unread {}, redispatch_refused false, executor calls 2, sealed null. No method patching or private object mutation is used. Depth 993 retained _RetainedHanding and correctly refused rollback.
findings.expected_result: Handed post-execution spend cannot disappear on restoration; redispatch must be refused and executor calls remain 1.
findings.proof: native.log records exact source identity and 22 deterministic native stack depths. The script is observational and exits 0 even when counterexample occurs; exit 0 is not a successful invariant check.
findings.trust_boundary: Uses public following callback, execution-side ledger replacement with owner-normalized checkpoint, and native stack exhaustion. It does not introspect/mutate execution-side private data, forge an authorization, or bypass admission. Execution owner is permitted to state a replacement checkpoint; reader promises forward-only observation.
findings.proposed_correction: Select an explicit owner-to-reader retention/lifetime or publication/acknowledgement contract guaranteeing that handed content remains available until authoritative capture. Implement acknowledgement only after stable native snapshot storage is retained. Alternative purely reader-local permanent refusal would violate the no-honest-poisoning invariant; bounded retries or fresh-stack capture can reduce this trigger but cannot guarantee recovery under repeat interruption plus mutable replacement.

architecture_decision_analysis.conclusion: Genuine handoff contract blocker for the full all-handed-spend guarantee under the stated interruption model, not proof that every bounded trigger needs architecture work.
architecture_decision_analysis.reason: After mutable mapping replacement and loss of every stable entry reference, recovered state is observationally identical to an unchanged honest account. Accepting it forgets spend; permanent retirement poisons the honest indistinguishable case; indefinite pending violates useful recovery. A reader implementation cannot reconstruct erased information. Fresh-stack retry can repair native stack exhaustion specifically but leaves asynchronous repeated pre-capture failure. Freezing/copying in the callback or requiring immutable transferred records is itself a selected lifetime/publication contract.
architecture_decision_analysis.exact_decision_required: Who retains each handed account version, until what explicit capture/compare acknowledgement, and which authority resolves recovery after interrupted publication? This can be a narrow execution-owner integration protocol rather than a second budget ledger or a new scientific authority.
